did: Laid out the project. One repository now holds both halves: cockpit, a Vite scaffold with React, TypeScript and ESLint, and api, beside docs and specs. I installed the cockpit's packages, added the flight feature's types file, moved App.tsx into src/app and added the API's entry file. Five commits, one at the end of each lesson that changed something.

evidence.label: Add docs folder and scaffold the cockpit app
Add the flight feature's types file
Add the API app entry file

fixes: Every lesson now says where the terminal starts and how to get there, and each folder step says at what level the folder goes
Explained the scaffolding tool's questions: answer y at "Ok to proceed?", choose ESLint at "Which linter to use?", and say no to installing and starting right away
Covered not having uv installed yet: make the api folder by hand and carry on
Explained the audit and funding lines after npm install, and the notice that a new version of npm is available
Marked the steps that only happen in the sandbox for learners working on their own machine
Replaced lesson 5's move commands with a drag-and-drop sorting drill, since those practice files only exist in the sandbox
Added a commit reminder to the end of each lesson, with a message and the files that should show up
learned: Where the terminal is decides where a new folder lands, and I had to stop and check more than once. Git doesn't record an empty folder, so a folder only shows up on GitHub once it has a file in it. I didn't have uv installed yet, so I made the api folder by hand and carried on.
title: Project structure: one repository, two apps
